## Research projects

### How much does meaning matter? A fresh look at grammatical alternations

*2021–2026 · PhD project, KU Leuven · FWO senior project G044721N*

How much do the meanings of the words involved shape the choice between grammatical variants, such as *give Mary the book* versus *give the book to Mary*? I developed a workflow that derives semantic predictors from vector-space models and integrates them into multivariate models of grammatical alternation. The workflow was applied to the English dative alternation, the future temporal reference alternation, and verbal complementation after *remember*, and was extended to English comparative adjectives during a research stay at the Université de Neuchâtel (2024). The data come from spoken and written corpora of English and Italian, including the Spoken BNC2014 and Switchboard. See the [dissertation page](PhD_dissertation.qmd) for more.

**Tools/Methods:** Python (Nephosem, UMAP), R (Rtsne, party, lme4, glmm)

[\[OSF research compendium\]](https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/52F94)

### WiGeDi: Wikidata Gender Diversity

*2021–2024 · Wikimedia Research Fund*

As a member of the research team, I studied how gender, including non-binary and queer identities, is represented in Wikidata and how that representation has changed over time. Part of this work involved a corpus-based analysis of the community discussions in which these modeling decisions are made. The project produced journal articles in *Internet Histories* and *Communication, Culture and Critique*, a book chapter in *Ethics in Linked Data*, and the WiGeTa-EN corpus of Wikipedia gender talks. In 2024, I co-organized the Queer Data Days.

**Tools/Methods:** Python, tidyverse

[\[WiGeTa-EN corpus\]](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20054893)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Exemplar modeling of derivational nonce formations in Italian (MA thesis)

*2019–2020 · University of Pisa and Utrecht University*

I applied a distributional exemplar model to Italian action nouns in -ATA, -ZIONE and -MENTO, treating the competing suffixes as a case of derivational overabundance with gradient, partly lexicalized preferences. During an Erasmus traineeship at UiL-OTS, Utrecht University (supervisor: Prof. D. Paperno), I built and annotated a dataset of Italian suffixed neologisms and nonce formations in CoNLL format. The project built on my BA thesis on Italian deverbal nouns in -ZIONE.

**Tools/Methods:** Python (fastText), cluster analysis, CoNLL annotation

[\[Annotated datasets\]](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20049797)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Ontology-based modeling of Dante's *Divina Commedia*

*2021 · ISTI-CNR "A. Faedo", Pisa · EU H2020 project ARIADNEplus*

As a graduate fellow, I designed an ontology-based data model for syntactic structures and metaphor in Dante's *Divina Commedia*, with structured annotation in XML and SQL.

**Tools/Methods:** ontologies, XML, SQL
